long_biography.plain_text:
Born in White Plains, New York, Mark Zuckerberg began writing software in childhood and studied computer science at Harvard. In 2004 he launched Facebook from his dormitory, initially for students, then moved to Palo Alto to build it full time. The network's expansion and 2012 public offering turned his founder stake into the core of his self-made fortune.

Facebook became Meta in 2021 as the company broadened beyond its original social network. Zuckerberg remains founder, chairman, chief executive and controlling shareholder; Meta's 2026 proxy records 60.8 percent of voting power through its dual-class share structure. His current strategy emphasizes artificial intelligence and immersive technologies. Beyond Meta, he co-leads the Chan Zuckerberg Initiative, which supports biomedical research, education and local communities with an increasingly technical approach to scientific discovery.
